• A “ribonucleoprotein particle” that meets a nascent polypeptide chain and tells it to “pause” is the signal-recognition particle (SRP).  
• SRP binds the emerging chain on a free ribosome in the cytosol and temporarily halts translation (“Pause there for a minute”).  
• SRP then guides the ribosome-nascent-chain complex to the rough endoplasmic reticulum (hence the pun “It seems somewhat rough”), where the chain is threaded into/through the ER membrane.  
• In the ER lumen the protein begins to be N-linked glycosylated (“you really need some sugar”).  
• After SRP releases, the chain continues its journey through the secretory pathway (ER → Golgi → vesicles) and is ultimately destined for secretion outside the cell (“I need to be on my way”).  

Thus the chain starts in the cytosol and is headed toward the extracellular space.

Answer: C
